description:
Found by defk-wfi.7, 2026-10-14, running the :sanitize tests on Linux for the first time.

Problem: with CC=clang (Debian clang 19.1.7, linux aarch64) and DEFK_SANITIZE=undefined, the kernel library fails to load: 'undefined symbol: __ubsan_handle_function_type_mismatch_abort'. On Linux, clang does not link the UBSan runtime into a shared object (macOS clang links its dylib runtime; gcc on Linux adds libubsan as a needed library, and its undefined mode passes).

Seen as: mix test test/sanitize_test.exs --include sanitize, test 'undefined: builds, loads its runtime itself, and the kernel runs' fails with CC=clang in the defk-ci:aarch64 image; 13/14 pass. The :sanitize tests are excluded by default, so CI does not show it.

Suspects/fix: add -shared-libsan for clang on Linux in Defk.Build's sanitizer flags (links libclang_rt.ubsan_standalone dynamically), or preload the runtime. Check the address mode too keeps passing (it does today, with LD_PRELOAD of libclang_rt.asan).

Done when: the undefined test passes with clang and gcc on Linux and on macOS.

comments.text:
Resolution: fixed, merged to main.
- Cause: clang off macOS does not link a sanitizer runtime into a shared object, so the kernel library had undefined __ubsan_* (or __asan_*) symbols. The address test hid it for ASan: clang -print-file-name=libasan.so finds gcc's libasan.so, which the test preloaded and which filled the symbols.
- Fix (lib/defk/build.ex, sanitize_flags/1): for clang off macOS and the address or undefined mode, add -shared-libsan and -Wl,-rpath,<clang's runtime dir> (from -print-libgcc-file-name --rtlib=compiler-rt; the loader does not search it). The flags are part of the cache key, so an old library is not reused.
- Test: the address test now preloads the compiler's own runtime (libclang_rt.asan-<arch>.so for clang, libasan.so for gcc): two ASan runtimes in one process abort ('Shadow memory range interleaves').
- CI image: ci/setup-debian.sh installs llvm, for llvm-symbolizer on the PATH; without it clang's ASan reports have no function names (addr2line as the symbolizer hung on the BEAM binary).
- Results: sanitize_test --include sanitize 14/14 on Linux aarch64 with clang and with gcc, and on macOS. macOS mix ci 1736/1736. Not run: x86-64 with --include sanitize (Rosetta; the :sanitize tests are excluded in CI).

title: [BUG] Sanitizer undefined mode with clang on Linux: the kernel library does not load
